issues.detail: The Greek 'ωμοιωθη' is a passive verb (it will be likened/compared), but the Vietnamese translates it as an active comparison ('giống như'). More importantly, the Greek 'ανθρωπω βασιλει' means 'a man [who] reigns as king', whereas the Vietnamese 'một người vua' simplifies the structure and misses the nuance of the reigning action.
The Greek 'οστις εποιησεν' (who did/made) is rendered as a simple description in the Vietnamese, slightly flattening the active nature of the action in the original.
